previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic migraines, pseudotumor cerebri, hypertension, diabetes, and anxiety was admitted after a fall associated with transient loss of consciousness. She had been experiencing a persistent headache for five weeks, poorly responsive to medications including amitriptyline and opioids. Evaluation revealed no acute intracranial or cardiopulmonary pathology. CT head and MRV were unremarkable except for a chronically narrow left transverse sinus. The fall was attributed to vasovagal syncope likely triggered by pain and polypharmacy. A treatment strategy was initiated to address possible medication-overuse headache, including discontinuation of opioids and amitriptyline, and a course of high-dose steroids transitioned to oral prednisone with taper. Propranolol was reduced, and topiramate was tapered due to kidney stone risk. Her pain stabilized, and she was discharged home with follow-up planned with her headache specialist.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo RHW with h/o migraines and idiopathic intracranial
hypertension, recently admitted for migraines, who presents with
recurrence of severe headache.
Current headache is similar to prior headaches and has no
concerning features for acute intracranial process. Though some
features are reportedly new, they are consistent with migraine
(eye pain and parethesias) and do not suggest concerning new
process. The headache ___ continue to represent multiple
etiologies, including migraine, medication related (previously
overuse, now withdrawal), and IIH (though less likely with 
recent
normal OP). Neuro exam is normal and reassuring, with only
subjective sensory changes in R forearm and hand without
particular localizable distribution.
Given limitation in options for treatment (cannot use NSAIDs or
narcotics), failure of recent treatment plan within 10 days of
discharge, we will it would be optimal to re-admit the patient
for reassesment of treatment plan. It ___ be that some of the
medications that were recently stopped were actually helping 
her,
or that steroids were tapered too quickly. We will try another
course of IV steroids as this seemed to work well last time, and
make further plans after speaking with outpatient providers. We
can also consider restarting Diamox now that she is off Topamax.
